proof_summary: For the candidate linear-recurrence sequence \(L\), the proof studies the defect \(f_k=L_{k+1}^2-L_{k+2}L_k\): its recurrence \(f_{k+3}=4f_{k+1}+f_k\), together with monotonicity and a growth bound for \(L\), inductively gives \(0<f_k\le L_k\). Hence \(L_{k+1}^2=L_{k+2}L_k+f_k\) has a positive remainder no larger than the denominator, so the ceiling-minus-one rule returns exactly \(L_{k+2}\); strong induction then identifies the originally defined sequence with \(L\).
